name: Swans
label: Homestead
lede: Michael Gira started Swans to make a room hurt, taught the band to sing, shut it down in 1997, and brought it back in 2010 with records that run two hours.

eras.title: Loud enough to hurt
eras.text: Michael Gira, a demolition worker with a bass, starts a band in a New York that is falling apart and aims it at the room. The first album is called Filth.

years.h: Michael Gira starts Swans with drummer Jonathan Kane
years.p: Gira sings and plays bass, Kane drums, and everyone else rotates: Sue Hanel on guitar, Mojo on tape loops, and a second bassist who might be Thurston Moore, Dan Braun or Jon Tessler.
years.xp:
Gira had moved to New York in 1979 and played in a band called Circus Mort first. He paid rent with construction work, including demolition, sheetrock and plastering, according to Wikipedia.

Kane later called Hanel "the most fearsome guitarist we'd ever heard in New York." She was gone before the band recorded, replaced by Bob Pezzola, and saxophonist Daniel Galli-Duani joined.

years.h: A first EP on Labor, blues chords in time that won't sit still
years.p: Gira, Kane, guitarist Bob Pezzola and saxophonist Daniel Galli-Duani make no wave with jazz instruments and time signatures that keep shifting.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the record as minimal chord structures rooted in blues, played on jazz instruments. Only Gira and Kane make it to the next record.

years.cap: Swans at CBGB, New York, April 22, 1983
years.h: Filth lands on Neutral and Swans stop being a curiosity
years.p: Norman Westberg arrives on guitar and Roli Mosimann on drums. The sessions ran in April 1983 at the Vanguard Records studio in New York.
years.xp:
Gira kept up the construction work while New York, in Wikipedia's words, sat in severe urban decay. His aim, as he put it: "I wanted the music to obliterate."

Robert Christgau's verdict: "Not only isn't it for everybody, it isn't for hardly nobody. I think it's a hoot."

years.h: Early shows come with police, and Gira goes after headbangers
years.p: The sets are painfully loud and sometimes end when the police show up. Gira steps on fingers resting on the stage, pulls hair, and hits headbangers he doesn't like.
years.xp: Wikipedia ties these run-ins with audiences to Gira's decision, in 1997, to end the band. After Children of God he said he was tired of the band's reputation for noise and of an audience that expected more of it.

eras.title: Slower, and then Jarboe
eras.text: Gira slows the band down and records Cop between New York and Zurich. Then Jarboe, who fell for Filth, turns up at rehearsal.

years.h: Cop slows everything down
years.p: Gira, Westberg, bassist Harry Crosby and Mosimann stretch the tempos and add tape loops, recording between the Vanguard studio in New York and Platinum in Zurich. It reaches number 12 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp: Recording ran February to May 1984. AllMusic's Ned Raggett called it "quite possibly one of the darkest recordings ever done". Wikipedia lists Godflesh, the Young Gods and Neurosis among the bands it shaped, and Terrorizer ranked it fourth on a 2011 list of the heaviest albums ever.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cop (album) · Wikipedia: Swans (band) · Discogs: Swans, Young God
years.h: The EP that names Gira's future label gets a US release on Homestead
years.p: Young God shares its title with the band's 1984 British release. The 1985 US pressing is on Homestead, according to Discogs.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes the EP came out alongside Cop and is known for its A-sides, including "I Crawled". Gira's voice turns slightly more melodic, with the snarl still in it.

years.cap: Michael Gira and bassist Algis Kizys at Mabuhay Gardens, San Francisco
years.h: Jarboe hears Filth and keeps turning up at rehearsal
years.p: She contacts Gira, sits in on rehearsals and auditions more than once before he takes her on.
years.xp:
She is credited as "scream" on the Time Is Money (Bastard) 12-inch. Bassist Algis Kizys joins in the same period.

Gira coached her singing, she told an interviewer: drop your consonants, and "sing like an American."

eras.title: The hammer goes down, MCA calls
eras.text: The hammer goes down and the piano comes out. A Joy Division cover catches on at college radio, and Gira takes a shot at MCA.

years.h: Greed is Jarboe's first record with the band
years.p: Drum machines and grand piano, out on K.422 in the UK and PVC in the US. It reaches number 6 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp: Recorded June to August 1985 at Intergalactic Studios in New York. The New York Times heard "hammer-on-anvil chording" and chanting voices "like some sinister religious ritual".

years.h: Holy Money lets Jarboe sing "You Need Me" and "A Hanging"
years.p: Cut in the same sessions as Greed and the A Screw single, it also reaches number 6 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes that Tool's Maynard James Keenan has cited it as a major influence.

years.src: Wikipedia: Public Castration Is a Good Idea
yt: Full set at the Paradiso, Amsterdam, February 22, 1986
years.h: Public Castration Is a Good Idea comes out as a semi-official bootleg
years.p: Taped at the ICA and ULU in London and The Garage in Nottingham, it's released on Some Bizzare with a video called A Long Slow Screw.
years.xp: The lineup was Gira, Westberg, Kizys, Jarboe, Ronaldo Gonzalez and drummer Ted Parsons. Thirsty Ear reissued it on CD in 1999.

years.h: Flute, oboe and cello arrive on Children of God
years.p: Six weeks at Sawmills Studios in Cornwall, with Jarboe now a full counterweight to Gira.
years.xp:
Gira's explanation for the turn: "By 1986/7 Swans had run its course with the physical assault of sound." Wikipedia says he feared the band would turn cartoonish if it kept going that way.

Caroline released it in the US and K.422 in the UK. Guests included oboist Lindsay Cooper, cellist Audrey Riley and flautist Simon Fraser.

years.h: Gira and Jarboe trade the lead on two albums as Skin
years.p: Blood, Women, Roses has Jarboe singing lead and Shame, Humility, Revenge has Gira, both slow, sparse and stripped down.
years.xp: The project is called Skin in Europe and World of Skin in the US, according to Wikipedia. A third album, Ten Songs for Another World, follows in 1990.

q: At last, I can make a living at what I love to do.
years.h: Swans cover Joy Division, and MCA calls
years.p: The Love Will Tear Us Apart single, sung by Gira on one version and Jarboe on another, becomes a US college radio hit and an offer from Uni/MCA.
years.xp: Gira, per Wikipedia: he had never seen any money from any of the band's records, and the offer felt like the payoff for years of work.

years.cap: Swans onstage at the Leadmill, Sheffield, July 1989
yt: Can't Find My Way Home, live at Club X, August 23, 1989
years.h: Bill Laswell produces Swans' one major-label album
years.p: Session players and folk textures replace the heavy guitar, and "Saved" reaches number 28 on the US alternative chart.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports it sold only around 5,000 copies in the UK, among the lowest figures in MCA's history, and was quickly deleted from the catalog. Gira later called the pairing with Laswell a mismatch, while admiring Laswell's wider work.

The album includes a cover of Steve Winwood's "Can't Find My Way Home".

eras.title: Young God, and the exit
eras.text: Back on independent footing, Gira starts Young God Records and makes four albums, the last a two-disc set cut from tapes going back to 1981. Then he calls it off.

years.h: Gira starts a label and borrows the name of an old EP
years.p: Young God Records begins as an outlet for Swans and later releases Angels of Light, Devendra Banhart, Akron/Family and Larkin Grimm, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: White Light from the Mouth of Infinity
years.h: White Light from the Mouth of Infinity opens the second half
years.p: Self-produced in New York, with Jarboe, guitarists Christoph Hahn and Nicky Skopelitis, and drummer Anton Fier.
years.xp: Recorded September 1990 to February 1991 at B. Monster. Wikipedia and Allmusic both treat it as the start of the second half of the band's career.

years.cap: Swans onstage at Bradford University, March 1992
years.h: Martin Bisi records Love of Life, the one without Westberg
years.p: It's the only Swans album of this stretch without Norman Westberg, and it comes with the Amnesia EP.

years.h: Melody moves to the front on The Great Annihilator
years.p: Recorded in New York and Chicago between February 1993 and June 1994, with a companion Gira solo album, Drainland.
years.xp: Jarboe co-composed two tracks. "Killing for Company" was inspired by the crimes of Dennis Nilsen, per Wikipedia. AllMusic called the album an epic; Trouser Press thought the band was running out of ideas.

years.h: Soundtracks for the Blind plays 1981 over 1985
years.p: Gira builds the 26-track, 141-minute double album from cassettes, surveillance tapes and multitrack sessions going back to 1981.
years.xp:
The title comes from recorded conversations with his blind father. Jarboe contributed surveillance tapes her FBI-agent father made of her childhood and her mother's dementia.

Gira's method, in his words: "I threw all those into the computer and assembled it that way." AllMusic's Ned Raggett called it "Swans' best album ever". Wikipedia gives the release date as October 29; the discography page says October 22.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swans (band) · Wikipedia: Swans Are Dead
years.h: The farewell tour ends, and Swans stop
years.p: Gira ends the band with one last studio album and a world tour, so other projects can have his time.
years.xp: The March 13 show at the Paradiso in Amsterdam is the main source for the live album Swans Are Dead.

eras.title: Angels of Light
eras.text: Gira keeps the label, drops the volume and starts Angels of Light. Swans exist as a live album and a memory.

years.h: Two Amsterdam nights, one live album
years.p: Disc one is mostly March 1997 at the Paradiso; disc two is the same room in August 1995.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes the 1995 disc was recorded with help from the Dutch radio station VPRO.

years.cap: Ticket stub for an Angels of Light show, June 23, 1999
years.h: Gira turns the volume down with Angels of Light
years.p: New Mother launches an acoustic-based band whose rotating cast later includes Kid Congo Powers, Kristof Hahn, Thor Harris and Phil Puleo.
years.xp: Angels of Light ran until 2009 and made albums including How I Loved You and We Are Him. Akron/Family became Gira's backing band and shared a split record with him in 2005.

eras.title: Swans are not dead
eras.text: An Angels of Light show convinces Gira to bring Swans back, and the big records that follow, three of them close to two hours each, are paid for by the fans.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swans (band) · Wikipedia: My Father Will Guide Me up a Rope to the Sky
years.h: "SWANS ARE NOT DEAD" appears on MySpace
years.p: Gira posts a new song on the Young God MySpace, and a comeback nobody saw coming is under way.
years.xp:
Gira traced the decision to an Angels of Light show about five years earlier, where he played "large chords that were very sustained and swaying, in this sort of slave-ship rhythm" and felt "a nascent urge right then to re-form or reinvigorate Swans."

The touring lineup was Gira, Kristof Hahn, Phil Puleo, Norman Westberg, Thor Harris and Christopher Pravdica. Jarboe was not part of it.

years.cap: Gira solo at the Doug Fir Lounge, Portland
years.src: Wikipedia: My Father Will Guide Me up a Rope to the Sky · Wikipedia: Swans (band)
years.h: My Father Will Guide Me up a Rope to the Sky pays for itself
years.p: Gira raises the money for the sessions by hand-making 1,000 copies of a solo demos album, I Am Not Insane.
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls selling out the signed, numbered copies an example of reverse financing: the proceeds from one project roll over to pay for the next.

The album was recorded in New York in 12-hour days, and it's the first Swans album without Jarboe since Greed. It scored 83 on Metacritic.

yt: Oxygen, live at Pitchfork Music Festival 2013
years.h: The Seer runs 119 minutes, and the title track takes 32 of them
years.p: Karen O sings on "Song for a Warrior", Jarboe returns on backing vocals, and Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker of Low sing on "Lunacy".
years.xp:
The live double album We Rose from Your Bed with the Sun in Our Head paid for it, along with personalized songs recorded for $500 donors. Gira called it "the culmination of every previous Swans album".

Pitchfork gave it 9.0 and wrote of its "magisterial grandeur and hypnotic allure". The A.V. Club's Jason Heller called the title track "the most harrowing, exhausting, cathartic, transcendental piece of music Gira has ever put to tape." It reached number 114 on the US Billboard 200.

years.h: To Be Kind becomes the highest-charting Swans album
years.p: It peaks at number 37 on the US Billboard 200 and 38 in the UK, and runs 121 minutes.
years.xp: Recorded at Sonic Ranch in Texas with producer John Congleton, with St. Vincent and Cold Specks as guests. Gira credits Bill Rieflin as "Honorary Swan Forever". Pitchfork scored it 9.2.

years.src: Pitchfork: Swans' Michael Gira Issues Statement · Wikipedia: Michael Gira
years.h: Larkin Grimm accuses Gira of rape; he denies it
years.p: Grimm alleges Gira raped her in 2008. Gira calls the encounter "an awkward mistake" and the accusation "a slanderous lie", per Pitchfork.
years.xp: Grimm, who had been on Gira's Young God label, said she never consented and that a no-sex agreement was part of her contract. Pitchfork's February 26, 2016 story carried Gira's statement and Grimm's reply.

years.h: The Glowing Man closes the trilogy
years.p: 118 minutes across two discs, recorded in seven places from Texas to Berlin, with Bill Rieflin credited as "Hitman and 7th Swan".
years.xp: Wikipedia says the album completes a three-part run with The Seer and To Be Kind, and that "The World Looks Red/The World Looks Black" reuses Gira's words from a 1983 Sonic Youth song with new music.

years.cap: Swans on The Glowing Man tour, October 2, 2017
years.h: The 2010 lineup plays its last shows
years.p: The Glowing Man turns out to be the last album from a mostly stable lineup, and after it Gira works with a revolving cast.
years.xp: Since 2019, Wikipedia says, Gira has toured and recorded with Swans as "a revolving cast of contributors".

eras.title: A revolving cast
eras.text: Gira keeps the name and swaps the people. Companion albums keep paying for the long ones.

years.cap: Michael Gira live at Caribbean Club, Kyiv, October 31, 2019
years.h: Leaving Meaning gets made in Berlin, Reykjavik, Albuquerque and Brooklyn
years.p: Baby Dee sings on "The Nub", the Necks and Anna von Hausswolff contribute, and Larry Mullins and Dana Schechter join the lineup.
years.xp: A March 2019 companion album, What Is This?, financed it. Pitchfork scored it 7.7.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bill Rieflin · Wikipedia: To Be Kind · Wikipedia: The Glowing Man
years.h: Bill Rieflin dies at 59
years.p: The drummer who played on Swans records for two decades dies of complications from stage 4 colon cancer, diagnosed in 2011, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Gira credited him as "Honorary Swan Forever" on To Be Kind and as "Hitman and 7th Swan" on The Glowing Man.

years.h: A companion album pays for The Beggar
years.p: Is There Really a Mind? funds a lockdown-written record cut May to August 2022 at Candy Bomber in Berlin, with Ben Frost as a guest.
years.xp: The CD cut runs 121 minutes. Gira says he decided to make Swans "a more open-ended venture, with musicians coming and going from project to project". Released on Mute and Young God.

years.h: Roli Mosimann dies at 68
years.p: The drummer on Filth and Cop dies of lung cancer in Wroclaw, Poland, according to Wikipedia; he later produced for the Young Gods and others.

years.h: Gira calls Birthing the last "big sound" Swans album
years.p: He built the material over a year on the road, then reworked it in the studio. Future records, he says, will be "significantly pared down".
years.xp: The lead single "I Am a Tower" runs 19 minutes. Metacritic scores it 87.
